title: Finite degree-zero and vanishing positive cohomology of the dense-open boundary
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a reduced curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a constructible etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open. Give its closed complement the reduced induced scheme structure, defined by the radical ideal of functions vanishing there, and write $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for this closed immersion. Let $B=i_*i^{-1}F$, with direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For the underlying abelian sheaf $B_{\mathrm{ab}}$, the group $H^0(X,B_{\mathrm{ab}})$ is finite and $H^q(X,B_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $q>0$, where cohomology is [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No prime annihilator or properness is assumed, and the empty complement is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, closed complement and finite stalk product; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GJA

proof.text: Since X is finite type over k, it is Noetherian. Its finitely many irreducible components have generic points in the dense open U. On each component the closed complement is a proper closed subset of a space of dimension at most one, so it is zero-dimensional. The reduced induced closed subscheme Z on the complement is therefore zero-dimensional and has finitely many closed points. The residue fields of these closed points are k. This includes the empty complement and zero-dimensional components, whose generic points must all lie in U.

The constructible module sheaf F has finitely generated stalk modules, hence finite stalks because Lambda is finite. Pullback to Z has those same geometric stalks. The zero-dimensional cohomology theorem identifies its degree-zero cohomology with their finite product and makes all positive-degree cohomology zero.

The closed immersion i:Z to X is finite. Its direct image is exact, and the Leray identification carries the cohomology of i_*i^*F on X to that of i^*F on Z. Forgetting to abelian sheaves commutes with the direct image and inverse image comparison. Thus the underlying abelian boundary sheaf has finite H^0 and zero H^q for q positive. For the empty complement the finite product is the zero group.

lean.statement: theorem dense_open_boundary_cohomology (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [IsReduced X] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) [Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf F] (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)) : let I := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal U.compl let B := (I.subschemeι)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj ((I.subschemeι)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj F) let B' := (sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj B Finite (Sheaf.H B' 0) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H B' q))
